title: Double-buy race: the already-sniped check runs many awaits before the row is written and is never repeated inside the nonce lock, so two concurrent handlers for one token both buy

evidence.note: V2 dedup: isTokenSniped is read once at handler start
isTokenSniped = SELECT 1 FROM trades WHERE token=? AND chain=? — true only once a row exists
V2 row is inserted only after submitBuyTx returned (many awaits after the check)
V3 row is inserted only after submit
submitBuyTx serializes submits through withNonceLock but nothing re-checks isTokenSniped inside the lock: the second handler waits for the lock, then buys again
V3 handler awaits waitForLiquidity (up to 30 s) before its buy, widening the window against a V2 handler for the same token
Telegram alpha drop calls handleNewPairForChain directly, concurrently with any factory event for the same pair
one address is routed to every matching chain context without awaiting

V2 HTTP poll: async setInterval callback with no in-flight guard; lastBlock is advanced only after queryFilter and the loop (:1647), so a cycle slower than 2 s lets the next cycle query the same block range and dispatch the same PairCreated twice
getTradeIdForPendingToken orders by second-resolution timestamp, so two rows of one token in one second are ambiguous (AUD-BUY-020)
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Concurrent signals can buy the same token repeatedly

sibling_sites_checked: Both handler entry checks (bot.ts:881, :1211) and both inserts (:1127, :1451) checked. Concurrency sources found: V2 PairCreated and V3 PoolCreated for one token; the same token on two V2 DEXes of a chain; Telegram alpha routing (telegramListener.ts:120-124 -> alphaDrop.ts:36/:47) concurrent with factory events; overlapping HTTP-poll cycles (:1636-1651, :1660-1676); duplicate listeners after dashboard stop/start or a WS drop (AUD-BUY-008, AUD-BUY-011). The deliberate path has a separate structural guard (nonce + balance delta, :617-662) and is not affected by this race within one process. The risk-gate race across DIFFERENT tokens is a separate mechanism, AUD-BUY-010.
severity_rationale: S1, equal to the research suggestion. The check-then-act gap and the concurrent dispatch sources are visible in code; a double buy spends twice the configured amount on one token (OVERSPEND), and the second position is then mis-linked (AUD-BUY-020).
recommendation: Phase 24: claim the token synchronously (before the first await) in an in-process set keyed by chain+token, and re-check the claim and the DB inside the nonce lock before submitting; release the claim on a genuine fail-clean. The exact mechanism and whether risk budget is reserved at the same time is card BUY-03. Nothing is changed in Phase 22.
